broker.name: Pepperstone
broker.tagline: On its own site since 2010. Its site names 8 regulators, including ASIC, FCA, and CySEC. Rules depend on where you live. Advertised leverage: Up to 1:1000.
broker.about: Pepperstone says it has operated since 2010. The pages checked do not name one headquarters. Account names on its site include Standard and Razor. Platforms named there include Pepperstone platform and mobile app, MetaTrader 4, MetaTrader 5, cTrader, and TradingView. The site names these regulators: ASIC, FCA, CySEC, BaFin, DFSA, CMA, SCB, and CMA (Kenya). The company on an account depends on where the client lives. Minimum deposit is not a single number on the pages that loaded. The highest leverage figure taken from those pages is Up to 1:1000. Leverage increases losses as well as gains.
broker.regulators_note: The company behind an account depends on where you live. ASIC: Pepperstone Group Limited, AFSL 414530. FCA: Pepperstone Limited, 684312. CySEC: Pepperstone EU Ltd, 388/20. BaFin: Pepperstone GmbH, 151148. DFSA: Pepperstone Financial Services (DIFC) Ltd, F004356. CMA: Pepperstone Financial Services LLC, 20200000358. SCB: Pepperstone Markets Limited, SIA-F217. CMA (Kenya).

plans.billing_note: Spreads from 0.1 pips. No commission except share CFDs. Share CFDs from 0.2% per side on Hong Kong share CFDs. Retail leverage 30:1, Pro 500:1.

broker.leverage_note: Leverage increases losses as well as gains, and you can lose more than you deposit. The highest figure on this card is the highest number this broker advertises. It is not the cap on every account. The cap depends on the company, the product and where you live.

other_fees.label: Minimum deposit
other_fees.note: The global accounts table shows a minimum deposit of $0 for both Standard and Razor. The same page says there is no obligation to fund the account, but when you do, the minimum you can add is $10 or your local equivalent. That is more than one number, and it changes with local currency.

other_fees.label: Inactivity fee
other_fees.note: The accounts page says Pepperstone does not charge an inactivity fee, and that there are no market-data fees.

other_fees.label: Overnight funding
other_fees.note: Applied for CFD positions held past 11:59 pm server time, described as 5 pm New York time. Not charged on futures or forwards.

_notes.fetch_notes: https://pepperstone.com timed out. Regional pages on the same domain loaded. The EU who-we-are page says Pepperstone was founded in 2010 in Melbourne, Australia, and that it has 12 global offices. It does not name a current headquarters, so headquarters is null. That page lists SCA with no country, entity or licence number. The Kenya CMA is named on the licence FAQ with no entity or licence number. The UAE CMA licence on the AE about page is for Introduction and Financial Consultation. TradingView is described as not available on a Standard CFD account in one answer, while the comparison table does not list TradingView for either account. The homepage risk warning on the accounts page says 80% of retail investor accounts lose money when trading CFDs with this provider. No client deposit promotion was stated.
